```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5,
                      dpi = 120)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse); library(here); library(rstan); library(splines)
  library(knitr); library(kableExtra); library(patchwork)
})
source(here("scripts", "dim_irt_helpers.R"))

# pre-fix helpers, straight from git, to rebuild exactly what the old fits saw
old <- new.env()
old_src <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines(system2("git", c("-C", here(), "show",
                            paste0(params$old_commit, ":scripts/dim_irt_helpers.R")),
                   stdout = TRUE), old_src)
sys.source(old_src, envir = old)

# two-series palette (validated: CVD dE 24.7, normal-vision dE 33.6); shape is the
# redundant channel so identity never rests on colour alone
pal   <- c("Before fix" = "#eb6834", "After fix" = "#2a78d6",
           "After fix, all visits" = "#1baf7a")
shp   <- c("Before fix" = 17, "After fix" = 16, "After fix, all visits" = 15)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
        legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position = "plot"))

fmt_ci <- function(x, d = 2) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f [%.", d, "f, %.", d, "f]"),
                                     median(x), quantile(x, .025), quantile(x, .975))
```

```{r data}
item_table <- build_item_table(readRDS(here("data", "items.rds")), load_instruments())
df_demogs  <- readRDS(here("data", "demographics.rds"))

pairs <- tribble(
  ~pair,                ~lang_a,              ~lang_b,              ~short,
  "EN (Am) × ES (Mex)",  "English (American)", "Spanish (Mexican)",  "EN-SP",
  "EN (Br) × ES (Eur)",  "English (British)",  "Spanish (European)", "ENGB-ESEU",
  "Norwegian × Polish",  "Norwegian",          "Polish",             "NO-PL"
)

# each pair, built three ways: the old collapsed matrix, latest admin, all admins
built <- pairs |> mutate(data = map2(lang_a, lang_b, \(a, b) {
  langs <- c(a, b)
  list(
    old    = suppressWarnings(old$build_pair_matrix(item_table, df_demogs, langs)),
    latest = suppressMessages(build_pair_long(item_table, df_demogs, langs, admins = "latest")),
    all    = suppressMessages(build_pair_long(item_table, df_demogs, langs, admins = "all"))
  )
}))
names(built$data) <- built$short
dataset_of <- df_demogs |> distinct(child_id = as.character(child_id), dataset_name)
```

# Summary

```{r fits-registry}
# every fit the report knows about; new fits live in this branch's models/
fits <- tribble(
  ~short,      ~version,                 ~file,                                                   ~thin, ~age_df, ~new,
  "EN-SP",     "Before fix",             "o5_bayes_full_EN-SP-1665items.rds",                     1,     3L,      FALSE,
  "EN-SP",     "After fix",              "o5_bayes_EN-SP-latest-thin3_fit.rds",                   3,     3L,      TRUE,
  "EN-SP",     "After fix, all visits",  "o5_bayes_EN-SP-all-thin3_fit.rds",                      3,     3L,      TRUE,
  "ENGB-ESEU", "Before fix",             "o5_bayes_full_English..British..rds",                   2,     1L,      FALSE,
  "ENGB-ESEU", "After fix",              "o5_bayes_ENGB-ESEU-latest-thin2_fit.rds",               2,     3L,      TRUE,
  "NO-PL",     "Before fix",             "o5_bayes_full_Norwegian-Polish.rds",                    2,     3L,      FALSE,
  "NO-PL",     "After fix",              "o5_bayes_NO-PL-latest-thin2_fit.rds",                   2,     3L,      TRUE
) |>
  mutate(path = if_else(new, here("models", file), file.path(params$old_models_dir, file)),
         available = file.exists(path)) |>
  left_join(pairs |> select(short, pair), by = "short")
```

```{r extract-draws}
# Posterior draws for the handful of parameters the report uses, cached so the
# multi-hundred-MB stanfit objects are only read once per new fit.
cache_file <- here("models", "o5_longitudinal_report_cache.rds")
cache <- if (file.exists(cache_file) && !params$refresh_cache) readRDS(cache_file) else list()

old_age_basis <- function(short, thin, df) {
  op <- built$data[[short]]$old
  keep <- op$item_lookup |> group_by(language) |>
    filter(row_number() %% thin == 0) |> pull(uid)
  obs <- old$wide_to_long_obs(op$resp[, keep, drop = FALSE],
                              op$item_lookup |> filter(uid %in% keep), op$covdata)
  x <- as.numeric(scale(obs$age))
  list(mean = mean(obs$age), sd = sd(obs$age), ns = if (df > 1) ns(x, df = df))
}

for (k in which(fits$available)) {
  key <- fits$file[k]
  if (!is.null(cache[[key]]) && cache[[key]]$mtime == file.mtime(fits$path[k])) next
  fit <- readRDS(fits$path[k])
  dr  <- as.data.frame(fit)
  keep <- grep("^(rho|ecv|lambda_g|c_shared|sigma_s|sigma_admin|beta_exp|beta_age|beta_age_exp)(\\[|$)",
               names(dr), value = TRUE)
  basis <- if (fits$new[k]) {
    readRDS(sub("_fit\\.rds$", "_prep.rds", fits$path[k]))$age_basis
  } else old_age_basis(fits$short[k], fits$thin[k], fits$age_df[k])
  sm <- summary(fit)$summary
  cache[[key]] <- list(
    mtime = file.mtime(fits$path[k]), draws = dr[, keep], basis = basis,
    diag = tibble(divergences = get_num_divergent(fit),
                  max_rhat = max(sm[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  min_neff = min(sm[c("rho", "ecv"), "n_eff"]),
                  hours = max(rowSums(get_elapsed_time(fit))) / 3600,
                  N = if (fits$new[k]) readRDS(sub("_fit\\.rds$", "_prep.rds", fits$path[k]))$data$N
                      else NA_integer_))
  rm(fit, dr); gc()
}
saveRDS(cache, cache_file)

draws_of <- function(file) cache[[file]]$draws
c_shared_of <- function(d) if ("c_shared" %in% names(d)) d$c_shared else d$lambda_g^2
done <- fits |> filter(available)
```

```{r headline-numbers}
rho_med <- function(short, version) {
  f <- done |> filter(short == !!short, version == !!version)
  if (!nrow(f)) return(NA_real_)
  median(draws_of(f$file)$rho)
}
r_old_ensp <- with(built$data[["EN-SP"]]$old,
  cor(covdata$age, rowMeans(resp, na.rm = TRUE)))
r_new_ensp <- built$data[["EN-SP"]]$all$obs |>
  group_by(admin_id, age) |> summarise(p = mean(y), .groups = "drop") |>
  with(cor(age, p))
pending <- fits |> filter(!available) |> mutate(label = paste0(pair, " — ", version))
```

- **The bug.** `build_pair_matrix()` collapsed each child's CDI administrations to
  "ever produced" (`max()` across visits) and gave every response a single
  child-level age. In the longitudinal English (American) × Spanish (Mexican)
  sample this erased the age signal: the correlation between age and proportion of
  items produced was **`r sprintf("%.2f", r_old_ensp)`**, against
  **`r sprintf("%.2f", r_new_ensp)`** when each administration keeps its own age.
- **The fix.** One row per (child, administration, item), each with its own age
  and exposure record (`build_pair_long()`); the Stan model takes per-observation
  exposure and, when visits repeat, a per-visit ability deviation.
- **The consequence.** For EN (Am) × ES (Mex) the cross-language ability
  correlation `rho` falls from
  **`r sprintf("%.2f", rho_med("EN-SP", "Before fix"))`** to
  **`r sprintf("%.2f", rho_med("EN-SP", "After fix"))`**: age-driven growth,
  shared by both languages, had been absorbed into the shared factor. The two
  cross-sectional samples barely move
  (Norwegian × Polish `r sprintf("%.2f", rho_med("NO-PL", "Before fix"))` →
  `r sprintf("%.2f", rho_med("NO-PL", "After fix"))`). Every sample still rejects
  both a single lexicon (`rho` = 1) and independent lexicons (`rho` = 0).
`r if (nrow(av <- done |> filter(short == "EN-SP", version == "After fix, all visits"))) paste0("- **All visits.** Using every EN (Am) × ES (Mex) visit, children's *stable* abilities correlate at **", sprintf("%.2f", median(draws_of(av$file)$rho)), "**; the correlation implied for a single visit matches the latest-visit fit (see §4).") else ""`
`r if (nrow(pending)) paste0("- **Pending fits** (shown as missing below; re-knit when they finish): ", paste(pending$label, collapse = "; "), ".") else ""`

# 1. The data: how longitudinal is each sample?

```{r admin-structure}
built |>
  transmute(pair, d = data) |>
  mutate(stats = map(d, \(x) {
    adm <- x$all$admins
    per_cell <- adm |> count(child_id, language)
    tibble(children = n_distinct(adm$child_id),
           administrations = nrow(adm),
           `children with a repeat visit` = n_distinct(per_cell$child_id[per_cell$n > 1]),
           `max visits / language` = max(per_cell$n),
           `age range (months)` = sprintf("%.0f–%.0f", min(adm$age), max(adm$age)))
  })) |>
  select(-d) |> unnest(stats) |>
  kable(align = "lrrrrr", caption = "Administrations per sample (children with every language of the pair).") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

Only English (American) × Spanish (Mexican) is substantially longitudinal. Its
children come from several studies with different designs:

```{r ensp-datasets}
built$data[["EN-SP"]]$all$admins |>
  group_by(dataset_name) |>
  summarise(children = n_distinct(child_id),
            administrations = n(),
            `visits per child (max)` = max(table(paste(child_id, language))),
            `age range` = sprintf("%.0f–%.0f", min(age), max(age)), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "EN (Am) × ES (Mex) by source dataset.") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

# 2. The problem: age carried no signal

Before the fix, each child appears once, with the proportion of items they
*ever* produced across all visits, plotted at a single child-level age (the
first exposure record's, median-imputed when missing — the vertical stripe at 30
months). After the fix, every administration is its own point at its own age.

```{r age-vocab-plot, fig.height = 5}
ensp <- built$data[["EN-SP"]]
before <- ensp$old$covdata |>
  mutate(prop = rowMeans(ensp$old$resp, na.rm = TRUE), version = "Before fix")
after <- ensp$all$obs |>
  group_by(child_id, admin_id, age) |>
  summarise(prop = mean(y), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(version = "After fix")
bind_rows(before, after) |>
  left_join(dataset_of, by = "child_id") |>
  mutate(version = factor(version, c("Before fix", "After fix"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(age, prop, colour = version, shape = version)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9, span = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~version) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) + scale_shape_manual(values = shp) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Age (months)", y = "Items produced (share of form)",
       title = "EN (Am) × ES (Mex): proportion of items produced vs. age",
       subtitle = "Before: one point per child (visits collapsed). After: one point per administration.") +
  guides(colour = "none", shape = "none")
```

```{r age-vocab-table}
cor_by_dataset <- function(df) df |>
  left_join(dataset_of, by = "child_id") |>
  group_by(dataset_name) |> summarise(r = cor(age, prop), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  bind_rows(tibble(dataset_name = "All datasets", r = cor(df$age, df$prop), n = nrow(df)))
full_join(cor_by_dataset(before) |> rename(`r before` = r, `n children` = n),
          cor_by_dataset(after)  |> rename(`r after` = r, `n administrations` = n),
          by = "dataset_name") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("r "), \(x) sprintf("%.2f", x))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Dataset", "r(age, vocab) before", "n children",
                      "r(age, vocab) after", "n administrations"),
        align = "lrrrr",
        caption = "Correlation of age with proportion produced, EN (Am) × ES (Mex).") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  row_spec(6, bold = TRUE)
```

The negative within-Hoff correlation before the fix is the giveaway: children
recruited young have more later visits to accumulate "ever produced" words, yet
were assigned their young first age.

# 3. The fix

- **`build_pair_long()`** — one row per (child, administration, item) with that
  administration's `age` and `admin_id` (`data_id`). `admins = "all"` keeps every
  visit; `admins = "latest"` keeps the oldest-age administration per child ×
  language (cross-sectional). Administrations with no recorded age are dropped
  rather than median-imputed.
- **`admin_language_exposure()`** — exposure from each administration's own
  record (it changes across visits for some children).
  `child_language_exposure()` is now its child-level mean.
- **Stan model** (`models/bilingual_dim_irt.stan`) — exposure enters per
  observation; with repeat visits (`estimate_admin`), child ability
  `theta_child[i, l]` (which defines `rho` / ECV) is shared across a child's visits
  and each visit adds a deviation `sigma_admin[l] · z_admin[a]`. The likelihood is
  vectorised.
- **`build_pair_matrix()`** (wide, for the mIRT route in 08 and the simulator in 10)
  now uses the latest administration per child × language — never a collapse.

The headline refits use `admins = "latest"`, the cross-sectional design the model
was built for, with each child's correct age. The all-visits variant asks a
slightly different question (the correlation of children's *stable* abilities).

```{r health}
            `% children with exposure` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * exposure_coverage)) |>

```

# 4. Results: cross-language ability correlation

```{r rho-forest, fig.height = 3.6}
rho_tbl <- done |>
  mutate(d = map(file, draws_of),
         rho_med = map_dbl(d, \(x) median(x$rho)),
         lo = map_dbl(d, \(x) quantile(x$rho, .025)),
         hi = map_dbl(d, \(x) quantile(x$rho, .975))) |>
  mutate(version = factor(version, names(pal)),
         pair = factor(pair, rev(pairs$pair)))
ggplot(rho_tbl, aes(rho_med, pair, colour = version, shape = version)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0, 1), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), linewidth = 0.9,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shp, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, .2)) +
  labs(x = expression(rho~"(posterior median, 95% CI)"), y = NULL,
       title = "Correlation of the two language abilities",
       subtitle = "0 = independent lexicons, 1 = a single lexicon",
       caption = if (any(rho_tbl$version == "After fix, all visits"))
         "All visits: correlation of stable (across-visit) abilities; the other estimates are per visit.")
```

```{r results-table}
param_row <- function(d) {
  tibble(rho = fmt_ci(d$rho), ECV = fmt_ci(d$ecv),
         c_shared = fmt_ci(c_shared_of(d)),
         `sigma_s (L1)` = fmt_ci(d$`sigma_s[1]`), `sigma_s (L2)` = fmt_ci(d$`sigma_s[2]`),
         `sigma_admin (L1 / L2)` = if ("sigma_admin[1]" %in% names(d) && any(d$`sigma_admin[1]` > 0))
           sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", median(d$`sigma_admin[1]`), median(d$`sigma_admin[2]`)) else "—")
}
done |>
  mutate(row = map(file, \(f) param_row(draws_of(f)))) |>
  select(pair, version, row) |> unnest(row) |>
  kable(caption = "Variance components (posterior median [95% CI]). L1/L2 = first/second language of the pair.") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12) |>
  collapse_rows(1, valign = "top")
```

```{r all-visits}
# In the all-visits model a single visit's ability is stable part + visit deviation,
# so the per-visit correlation is c_shared / sqrt(v1 v2) with v_l including sigma_admin^2
av <- done |> filter(short == "EN-SP", version == "After fix, all visits")
if (nrow(av)) {
  d  <- draws_of(av$file)
  v1 <- d$c_shared + d$`sigma_s[1]`^2 + d$`sigma_admin[1]`^2
  v2 <- d$c_shared + d$`sigma_s[2]`^2 + d$`sigma_admin[2]`^2
  av_rho_visit  <- fmt_ci(d$c_shared / sqrt(v1 * v2))
  av_rho_stable <- fmt_ci(d$rho)
  av_stable_share <- sprintf("%.0f%% / %.0f%%",
    100 * median((d$c_shared + d$`sigma_s[1]`^2) / v1),
    100 * median((d$c_shared + d$`sigma_s[2]`^2) / v2))
}
```

```{r all-visits-text, results = "asis"}
if (nrow(av)) cat(paste0(
  "## Stable vs. single-visit correlation (EN (Am) × ES (Mex), all visits)\n\n",
  "The all-visits fit splits each visit's ability into a stable child-level part ",
  "and a visit-specific deviation (`sigma_admin`), independent across the two ",
  "languages. Its `rho` = **", av_rho_stable, "** is the correlation of children's ",
  "*stable* English and Spanish abilities. The correlation it implies for a *single* ",
  "visit, where the deviation is included, is **", av_rho_visit, "**. That agrees ",
  "with the latest-visit fit, so the two designs are consistent. The stable part is ",
  av_stable_share, " (English / Spanish) of a single visit's age- and ",
  "exposure-adjusted ability variance. Single-visit figures are the like-for-like ",
  "comparison with the cross-sectional samples (EN (Br) × ES (Eur), NO × PL), where ",
  "stable and visit-specific variance cannot be separated.\n"))
```

## Why `rho` fell for EN (Am) × ES (Mex)

The shared covariance `c_shared` roughly halves while the language-specific
variances `sigma_s` barely change. A descriptive analogue makes the mechanism
visible without the IRT model: correlate each child's English and Spanish
vocabulary (logit proportion produced) after regressing out exposure, with and
without also regressing out age.

```{r decomposition}
lg <- \(x) qlogis(pmin(pmax(x, 0.005), 0.995))
partial_r <- function(d, exp_tbl, age_adj) {
  d <- d |> left_join(exp_tbl, by = c("child_id", "language")) |>
    group_by(language) |> mutate(e = coalesce(e, median(e, na.rm = TRUE))) |> ungroup()
  f <- if (age_adj) v ~ e + ns(age, 3) else v ~ e
  r <- d |> group_by(language) |>
    mutate(res = resid(lm(f, data = pick(everything())))) |> ungroup() |>
    select(child_id, language, res) |> pivot_wider(names_from = language, values_from = res)
  cor(r[[2]], r[[3]], use = "complete.obs")
}
decomp <- pairs |> mutate(res = pmap(list(short, lang_a, lang_b), \(s, a, b) {
  x <- built$data[[s]]
  exp_tbl <- child_language_exposure(df_demogs, c(a, b)) |>
    select(child_id, language, e = exposure_proportion)
  oldv <- as_tibble(x$old$resp, rownames = "child_id") |>
    pivot_longer(-child_id, names_to = "uid", values_to = "y") |> filter(!is.na(y)) |>
    left_join(x$old$item_lookup |> select(uid, language), by = "uid") |>
    group_by(child_id, language) |> summarise(v = lg(mean(y)), .groups = "drop") |>
    left_join(x$old$covdata |> select(child_id, age), by = "child_id")
  latv <- x$latest$obs |> group_by(child_id, language) |>
    summarise(v = lg(mean(y)), age = mean(age), .groups = "drop")
  tibble(`Before fix: exposure` = partial_r(oldv, exp_tbl, FALSE),
         `Before fix: + age` = partial_r(oldv, exp_tbl, TRUE),
         `Latest visit: exposure` = partial_r(latv, exp_tbl, FALSE),
         `Latest visit: + age` = partial_r(latv, exp_tbl, TRUE))
})) |> select(pair, res) |> unnest(res)
decomp |>
  mutate(across(-pair, \(x) sprintf("%.2f", x))) |>
  kable(caption = "Partial correlation of L1 and L2 vocabulary (logit proportion produced), controlling for exposure, then also for a natural-spline age term.") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Visits collapsed, child-level age" = 2,
                     "Latest administration, its own age" = 2))
```

Adjusting for age lowers the cross-language correlation in every sample, because
age-driven growth raises both languages together. In the two cross-sectional
pairs that adjustment was always possible (their ages were right), so the
before/after columns barely differ. In EN (Am) × ES (Mex) before the fix,
"adjusting for age" did almost nothing, because the age it was given carried no
signal; with each administration's real age the adjustment takes effect. That
accounts for most of the drop; a smaller part comes from using one administration
rather than "ever produced".

# 5. Age and exposure effects

The age effect on ability (the natural-spline term), shown relative to 24 months.
Before the fix the EN (Am) × ES (Mex) curve was U-shaped — 18-month-olds above
24-month-olds — and the EN (Br) × ES (Eur) fit predated the spline (linear age).

```{r age-curves, fig.height = 4}
curve_tbl <- done |>
  mutate(cur = pmap(list(short, file), \(s, f) {
    rng <- quantile(built$data[[s]]$latest$admins$age, c(.05, .95))
    ages <- seq(floor(rng[1]), ceiling(rng[2]), by = 0.5)
    ages <- sort(unique(c(ages, 24)))
    d <- draws_of(f)
    ba <- as.matrix(d[, grep("^beta_age(\\[|$)", names(d)), drop = FALSE])
    m <- age_effect_draws(cache[[f]]$basis, ba, ages)
    m <- m - m[, ages == 24]
    tibble(age = ages, med = apply(m, 2, median),
           lo = apply(m, 2, quantile, .025), hi = apply(m, 2, quantile, .975))
  })) |>
  select(pair, version, cur) |> unnest(cur) |>
  mutate(version = factor(version, names(pal)), pair = factor(pair, pairs$pair))
ggplot(curve_tbl, aes(age, med, colour = version, fill = version)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = version), linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~pair, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) + scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Before fix" = "22", "After fix" = "solid",
                                   "After fix, all visits" = "41")) +
  labs(x = "Age (months)", y = "Ability relative to 24 months (logits)",
       title = "Fitted age effect on lexical ability",
       subtitle = "Posterior median and 95% band; each fit's own age range (5th–95th percentile)")
```

```{r exposure-table}
done |>
  mutate(row = map(file, \(f) {
    d <- draws_of(f); sdv <- cache[[f]]$basis$sd
    tibble(`beta_exp (L1)` = fmt_ci(d$`beta_exp[1]`), `beta_exp (L2)` = fmt_ci(d$`beta_exp[2]`),
           `age × exposure (L1), per month` = fmt_ci(d$`beta_age_exp[1]` / sdv),
           `age × exposure (L2), per month` = fmt_ci(d$`beta_age_exp[2]` / sdv))
  })) |>
  select(pair, version, row) |> unnest(row) |>
  kable(caption = "Exposure main effects (centred exposure proportion) and the age × exposure interaction, rescaled to per-month.") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12) |>
  collapse_rows(1, valign = "top")
```

Exposure remains the dominant driver of *which* language's words a child
produces, and its main effect is essentially unchanged by the fix.

# 6. Convergence

```{r diagnostics}
done |>
  mutate(dg = map(file, \(f) cache[[f]]$diag)) |>
  select(pair, version, thin, dg) |> unnest(dg) |>
  transmute(pair, version, `items kept` = paste0("1 in ", thin),
            observations = if_else(is.na(N), "—", format(N, big.mark = ",")),
            divergences, `max R-hat` = sprintf("%.3f", max_rhat),
            `min n_eff (rho, ECV)` = round(min_neff),
            `sampling time (h)` = sprintf("%.1f", hours)) |>
  kable(caption = "4 chains × (1000 warmup + 1000 sampling) unless noted; max R-hat over all saved parameters.") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12) |>
  collapse_rows(1, valign = "top")
```

# 7. Caveats and open items

- **Comparisons are not perfectly like-for-like.** The pre-fix EN (Am) × ES (Mex)
  reference is the full 1665-item fit with concept linking; the corrected fit uses
  1 in 3 items without linking. On the pre-fix data, thinning and linking did not
  move `rho` (0.585 thinned vs 0.587 full), but that check has not been repeated on
  the corrected data. The pre-fix EN (Br) × ES (Eur) fit used a linear age term.
- **Repeated visits.** The headline corrected EN (Am) × ES (Mex) estimate uses
  each child's latest visit only. The all-visits model has no child-specific growth
  rates: growth differences go into the per-visit deviation `sigma_admin`. That
  deviation is also independent across the two languages, even when both CDIs were
  filled in at the same visit. A shared visit-level component (a growth spurt, or
  how the parent reported that day) is not modelled, so its effect on the
  stable-ability `rho` is unknown.
- **The EN–ES gap.** The two English–Spanish samples now differ clearly
  (0.40 vs ~0.7). The British/European sample has the higher CDI floor; the
  American/Mexican one the wider, longitudinal age range. Which drives the gap is
  unresolved.
- **Calibration.** The SBC recovery check in `09` used the pre-fix EN–SP design
  and has not been rerun.
`r if (nrow(pending)) paste0("- **Not yet fitted:** ", paste(pending$label, collapse = "; "), ". Re-knit after they finish; the cache picks up new fits automatically.") else ""`

# Reproducing

Data (`data/items.rds`, `data/demographics.rds`, `data/instruments/`) are
embargoed; this report shows aggregates only. New fits:

```
Rscript scripts/fit_dim_irt.R latest 3 EN-SP-latest-thin3
Rscript scripts/fit_dim_irt.R all    3 EN-SP-all-thin3
Rscript scripts/fit_dim_irt.R latest 2 ENGB-ESEU-latest-thin2 1000 1000 "English (British)" "Spanish (European)" 0
Rscript scripts/fit_dim_irt.R latest 2 NO-PL-latest-thin2     1000 1000 "Norwegian" "Polish"
```

Pre-fix fits are read from `params$old_models_dir`
(`r params$old_models_dir`), and the pre-fix pipeline is taken from git at
`r params$old_commit`.
